source: FICTIONAL desktop-PC maintenance simulation. Illustrative only - not real maintenance advice. Hardware facts to be validated against an equipment source before the main study.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU rocker switch at the rear of the case to O (off).
steps.explanation: The switch isolates mains power from the motherboard. The board still carries standby voltage while the switch is on, so nothing is touched before this.

steps.instruction: Touch the bare metal ground point to discharge static.
steps.explanation: Static electricity from your body can destroy the graphics card's memory without any visible spark. Grounding once, before the case is opened, covers the whole job.
The panel is held by four thumbscrews, one at each corner. They are hand-tight, so no tools are needed.
Each thumbscrew is loosened individually. Removing them one at a time keeps the panel seated until all four are free.
Thumbscrews stay captive in the panel, so they cannot roll into the case or get lost.
With the last screw free the panel is only held by the slots along the case edge.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel off to open the case.
steps.explanation: The panel rides on slots along the case edge. Sliding it back first, then lifting, avoids bending the sheet metal.

steps.instruction: Unplug the 8-pin PCIe power cable from the graphics card.
steps.explanation: The card draws up to 75 watts through the slot and the rest through this cable. The cable must come off before the card moves, or it drags the card and the socket.

steps.instruction: Press the retention latch at the back of the PCIe slot down.
steps.explanation: The latch locks the card's edge contacts into the slot. Releasing it frees the card; pulling without releasing can snap the latch.

steps.instruction: Lift the graphics card straight out of the slot.
steps.explanation: Straight up keeps the edge contacts aligned with the slot. Tilting while the contacts are still engaged scratches them.

steps.instruction: Seat the replacement card in the slot until the latch clicks.
steps.explanation: Even pressure across both ends of the card seats all the contacts at once. The latch clicking confirms it is locked.

steps.instruction: Plug the 8-pin PCIe power cable back into the graphics card.
steps.explanation: The connector is keyed so it only fits one way. A card without its power cable will not start.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel back on until it clicks home.
steps.explanation: Closing the case before power is restored keeps dust out and the airflow path intact.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU power switch back to I (on).
steps.explanation: Power is restored only after every part is secured, so the card can be enumerated cleanly during startup.

hazard.message: STATIC WARNING: charge detected on your wrist. Discharge on the case metal before touching the card!
